paper.title: Systems Design of Transformation Toughened Blast-Resistant Naval Hull Steels
paper.author: Arup Saha

evidence.claim: Carbon deliberately minimized for weldability
Stabilizes dispersed austenite for transformation toughening
Forms BCC precipitates and nucleates the Ni-stabilized austenite
Partitions Cu out of austenite into the precipitate phase
Primary M2C carbide former
Secondary M2C carbide former

processing.notes: Approximate solution treatment temperature reported in the dissertation.
Used to complete the martensitic/bainitic transformation before tempering.
First stage of the optimized multi-step secondary-hardening temper.
Second stage; this two-step schedule produced the best measured strength-toughness combination.

evidence.claim: ~3 nm particle size targeted as the Orowan-strengthening optimum
Observed at approximately 2-3 nm scale
Reported atom-probe observation of ~5 nm fine austenite nucleated on Cu precipitates
Design target range approximately 150-180 ksi (1034-1241 MPa)
Design objective: Charpy toughness above ~85 ft-lb (115 J)
Approximately 160 ksi (1100 MPa) measured on the prototype
Approximately 130 ft-lb (176 J) under the optimized multi-step temper
Ductile behavior reported above 90 ft-lb near -40C

weldability_indicators.notes: Carbon held well below the ~0.15 wt% rule-of-thumb weldability limit, at a direct cost to available M2C strengthening.

evidence.claim: Ni enrichment stabilizes dispersed austenite
Stress-induced austenite-to-martensite transformation absorbs energy at the crack tip
Cu precipitates give dislocation-obstruction strengthening
Ni-stabilized austenite preferentially nucleates on Cu precipitates
Cr shifts Cu out of austenite into the precipitate phase rather than aiding carbide strength directly
Mo and V are the primary M2C carbide formers

design_rationale: Low carbon (0.05 wt%) protects weldability at a direct cost to available M2C strengthening.
Ni stabilizes precipitated austenite for transformation toughening.
Cu serves a dual role: precipitation strengthening and austenite nucleation site.
Cr is added to partition Cu out of austenite into the precipitate phase, not for direct carbide strengthening.
Mo and V are tuned M2C carbide formers targeting a ~3 nm particle size for maximum precipitation strengthening.
